intro: When you search for a bridge near me, you are likely looking for a private dentist who can replace a missing tooth or teeth with a fixed bridge. A bridge is a common dental restoration that attaches false teeth to neighbouring teeth or implants. Finding a local professional who can assess your mouth and explain your options is the first step.
need_heading: What people searching for a bridge near me usually need
need_lead: Most people searching for a bridge near me want a local dentist who can replace missing teeth with a fixed solution.
needs: You have one or more missing teeth and want a fixed replacement that does not come out like a denture.
You have heard that a bridge might be quicker or less invasive than an implant and want to know if it suits your mouth.
You need a dentist close to home or work who can see you soon to discuss a bridge.
You are unsure whether an adhesive bridge or a conventional bridge is right for your gap and want a professional opinion.
You have an existing bridge that is loose, worn or uncomfortable and want a local dentist to assess it.
context_heading: Understanding bridges and your local options
context: A bridge replaces missing teeth by anchoring false teeth to the teeth on either side of the gap, or to dental implants. Some bridges are adhesive and need very little preparation of the neighbouring teeth, while others involve more reshaping. Your dentist will explain which type is suitable after examining your mouth.

Bridges need careful cleaning underneath to keep the supporting teeth and gums healthy. It is also worth comparing a bridge with an implant, as each has different advantages and maintenance needs. A local private dentist can talk you through both so you can decide what feels right for you.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Mention how many teeth are missing and where they are in your mouth, as this affects the type of bridge that may be possible.
Say whether you already have a bridge that needs replacing or repairing, and what the problem is.
Include your general location and how far you are willing to travel to see a dentist.
Note any preference you have for a particular type of bridge, such as adhesive or implant-supported, if you have one.
Mention if you have gum disease, as this can affect whether a bridge is suitable.
Say if you are looking for a private dentist specifically, as this is a private service introduction.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the dentist about a bridge
questions: What type of bridge would you recommend for my missing tooth or teeth, and why?
How much tooth preparation is involved with the bridge you are suggesting?
What are the alternatives to a bridge, such as an implant or denture, and how do they compare?
How should I clean under the bridge to keep it and my other teeth healthy?
How long might the bridge last, and what could make it need replacing?
What is the process from start to finish, including how many visits I will need?

faqs.q: Is a bridge better than an implant?
faqs.a: There is no simple answer, as it depends on your mouth, your health and your preferences. A bridge is fixed and may be quicker, while an implant avoids preparing neighbouring teeth. A dentist can compare the options for your situation.

faqs.q: Can I get a bridge on the NHS?
faqs.a: Some bridges are available on the NHS if you are eligible for NHS dental treatment and it is clinically appropriate. However, this service introduces you to private dentists, who will quote you directly for private treatment.

faqs.q: How do I check a dentist is qualified?
faqs.a: Dentists must be registered with the General Dental Council, and you can check the register online. Private clinics providing regulated healthcare in England must also register with the Care Quality Commission, which inspects and publishes ratings.

faqs.q: What if I have a problem with private dental treatment?
faqs.a: Start with the practice's complaints process. If it is not resolved, the Dental Complaints Service can help with private dental complaints.
